newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank data show 0.2 pct q/q fall in Q4 GDP.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank data show 0.2 pct q/q fall in Q4 GDP.

text.p: German economic output declined 0.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the previous quarter, data released by the Bundesbank on Thursday showed.

The Bundesbank initially produced a rounded figure showing zero growth for the quarter-on-quarter rate. But the slight contraction in the economy could be calculated from the raw data provided by the central bank.
Economists said the data were weaker than forecast, and that the sluggish 1996 rebound appeared to have sputtered to a halt in the fourth quarter.

They said the fourth-quarter data reinforced views that 1997 economic growth was likely to fall short of the government's projection of 2.5 percent although IFO business confidence data left some feeling more optimistic than previously on the 1997 outlook.
Weak consumer spending was the main reason for the fourth-quarter decline, while a surge in imports also outweighed a rise in exports, the economists said.

Gross domestic product (GDP) in the fourth quarter totaled 770.4 billion marks ($456.5 billion) in the quarter, down slightly from 772 billion marks the previous quarter, but 1.6-percent higher than the year-earlier quarter.
Growth in the third quarter was 0.8 percent from the previous quarter and 1.9 percent year-on-year.
"Private comsumption suffered from high unemployment and a small decline in disposable income," said analyst Holger Fahrinkrug at UBS in Frankfurt, who sees 1997 growth at 2.0 percent.
Robert Prior-Wandesforde at HSBC James Capel in London, who forecasts 1997 growth at 2.4 percent, said he did not expect the Bundesbank to be too alarmed by the data.
"The prospects for a reasonably strong bounce in activity from February/March (are) set to allay the worst fears that Germany is heading back into a prolonged period of weakness."
The IFO survey also released on Thursday points to an upturn in business confidence in January, both analysts noted.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.687 German Marks)
